themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Stated vision is "to offer an integrated technology platform to our customers in the travel and hospitality sector, powered by artificial intelligence, enabling them to increase their revenue through guest acquisition, retention, and wallet share expansion."
- Customer franchise cited as 25 Global Fortune 500 companies, 33 of the Top 40 hotel chains, all leading OTAs & Metas, 7 of Top 10 car rentals, 4 of Top 5 airlines, large cruise lines and the largest DMOs.
- Three business units with distinct stated Serviceable Addressable Markets: DaaS USD 1.1 Bn, Distribution USD 1.9 Bn, MarTech USD 5.8 Bn (source: company information, Phocuswright and 1Lattice report).
- Platform framed as covering the full traveller journey — Dreaming, Planning, Booking, Trip and Post-trip — with MarTech, DaaS and Distribution products mapped to each stage.
- Won "Best Company in AI-Powered Travel Marketing" (2026 Best in SaaS Award), described as "3 Years in a Row", and was named Emerging Company of the Year at The Economic Times Awards for Corporate Excellence.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Sojern (2025) is the defining event of the period — it is credited for the customer-count step-up to 14,158, the 47.3% headcount increase, MarTech growth of 341.2% Y-o-Y, and the deferred consideration charge running to Q3FY29; management frames the strategy as "Together with Sojern, we are focused on one outcome, helping travel and hospitality businesses grow faster".
- [Partnerships] New partnerships and wins named in the quarter: Philippine Airlines (competitive pricing intelligence), Duetto (autonomous real-time revenue optimization), Cinko (last-minute booking demand), ZentrumHub (connectivity), BoxPay (payments via RG Pay) and Citrus Leisure (UNO Direct Stack in Sri Lanka).
- [Exceptional item] The P&L shows Exceptional Expenses of INR 34.6 Cr in FY26 (nil in FY25 and nil in all quarters shown); the deck states FY26 Adj. PAT accounts for both the deferred deal consideration and a "One-time exceptional expense incurred in Q3FY26" but does not describe its nature.
- [Shareholding] Shareholder types as of June 30, 2026: Promoters & Promoter Group 48.78%, Mutual Funds 17.56%, FIIs 5.75%, Corporate Bodies 9.41%, Others 17.63%, Insurance Companies 0.87%; largest named non-promoter holders are Sundaram Mutual Fund 5.46% and Nippon Life India Mutual Fund 4.49%.
